The Battle of Baška Valley (in Italian: Battaglia della Valle Baccia) was a pitched battle fought on the right bank of the Isonzo, in present-day Slovenia, between June 29 and July 3, 1944, between the Army of the Italian Social Republic, supported by the Wehrmacht, and Yugoslav and Slovene partisans, during the World War II.
Background
During 1943, following the Allied invasion of Italy, as a consequence of the strengthening of Tito 's partisans, tensions at the gates of Friuli grew more and more.
In the Battle of Baška Valley, during the autumn of 1943, the Bersaglieri of the 1st "Mussolini" Battalion, belonging to the 8th Bersaglieri Regiment, were sent and distributed in various strongholds placed to defend the territory. From the very beginning, the young Bersaglieri had to face repeated attacks launched by the IX Korpus of the People's Liberation Army of Yugoslavia.
In the summer of 1944, the IX Korpus set itself the objective of expanding its movement zone, which was hindered by the presence of the railway line, which passed right through the middle of the partisan deployment, the latter being thus divided in two for a stretch of 20 km. A hypothetical annihilation of the Mussolini battalion would have led to the complete occupation of the Baška Grapa () by the Slovene Partisans, followed by a heavy moral blow to the Italians.
Forces
Gorizia–Podbrdo section
The stretch of road and railway from Gorizia to Podbrdo were controlled by 1,500 men, acoording to the Slovenians.
Most–Bovec–Tolmin section
A few hundred Italian Alpini covered the Most–Bovec–Tolmin pass. The great attack of the IX Slovenian Korpus took place at the end of June 1944 and developed from railway toll booth 92, around the Bača river, up to railway toll booth 107 near the Podbrdo tunnel.
Axis forces
The defensive deployment included 1,100 men of which 800 from the 1st "Mussolini" Bersaglieri Battalion and 200 from the Alpini Battalion "Val Tagliamento".
About 450 men were those who supported the great attack for 4 days.
According to Stanko Petelin, the defenders were around 500. While other sources claim that the attack was supported by 700 men.
Partisan forces
The attack took the defenders completely by surprise, who had never imagined an attack of such magnitude, the soldiers of the IX Korpus were masters in concealing their vehicles and logistics, to transport in total silence an attack force of between 5,000 and 7,000 men, including over 20 battalions. The Slovene Partisans included the "Kosovel", "Tržaška", "Bazoviška", "Gradnik", "Vojko" and "Preseran" brigades.
Battle
Initial Slovene attack
At 2 o'clock on June 29 the attack began. While the main parts of the "Kosovel" Brigade, supported by artillery, attacked Kneža, the 1st and 3rd Battalions were instead charged with conquering Clavice. The "Tržaška" Brigade attacked the toll booths 93 and 96 of the railway. In this sector the partisans concentrated their efforts using approximately 1,500 men, supported by 2 pieces of artillery, 4 47 mm cannons, 4 81 mm mortars, 12 light mortars. The assault on the Clavice station by the "Kosovel" brigade was unsuccessful, because the partisans were not familiar with the defences and encountered tangles of barbed wire on their way several times and, because of this, by dawn the Slovene Partisans had already suffered 10 casualties.
Meanwhile, in Podmelec the situation was unstable: 5 bersaglieri had been knocked out by a targeted artillery strike while another squad was surprised by the partisans and lost two men. On the other hand, 4 fallen partisans were found.
In Kneža the partisan artillery hit the whole surrounding area although with poor precision, in this sector the defenders suffered one casualty and 10 wounded while the attackers suffered heavy losses due above all to the 81mm mortar and the anti-aircraft gun defending the area, which hit the side of the Koncarje ridge.
From Most na Soči a truck was sent out with 1 officer and 7 riflemen, but when it reached Podmelec it was hit by partisan fire, the riflemen were almost all wounded and managed to find shelter in a house where they tried to resist, but once the partisans surrounded the house, the riflemen had no other solution than to surrender. The same people were made prisoners and were shot in Ponivke the same day. The partisans of the "Bazoviška" brigade and members of the 9th Korpus' artillery took part in the clash; due to the lack of further information it only appears that the partisans suffered one wounded during these battles.
Thus an improvised group of about forty sharpshooters and 20 Alpen Jager set out from Santa Lucia d'Isonzo, but the column was surprised by the Slovenian partisans and forced into battle. However, about twenty sharpshooters managed to disengage and reached toll booth 93 and continued on to Piedimelze, penetrating the deployment of the 19th "Kosovel" brigade, which found itself hit from behind and suffered several losses. In the operation, 2 fighters fell and several were wounded, including the commander of the brigade "Anton Sibelja-Stjenka".
Kosovel was badly damaged by the clash: hit from behind on more than one occasion, its battalions (1st and 3rd) retreated under enemy fire, failing to occupy Clavice.
The partisans soon attacked the fort of 93 which could count on about fifteen defenders who took refuge in the railway tunnel, the partisans attacked the entrances but were repelled and retreated momentarily because of an Italian patrol that surprised them from behind. The bersaglieri found only the body of an enemy; confirmed losses on the Slovenian side: 1 fallen and 1 seriously wounded.
According to the same Slovenian source on the "Kosovel" brigade, an enemy group even infiltrated the brigade headquarters causing serious damage and casualties to the brigade personnel, the situation was re-established thanks to a counterattack. There was a hard hand-to-hand clash from which the bersaglieri then disengaged; the episode was considered a real disaster from which the partisans learned for the future. 5 dead and 23 wounded were the toll of Kosovel during the clash that day.
The end of the day concluded with the assault on the "96" fort defended by 15 riflemen. The attack was launched by the Trieste Assault Brigade. the clash was however a hard moral blow dealt to the "Triestine" attackers who initially found themselves in the advantage, to the point that they almost managed to make the enemy position capitulate but were then surprised from behind in an elevated position by a group of 6 Alpen Jager and 20 riflemen, who directed the fire of a mortar on the attackers. The partisans overestimated the enemy strength and retreated abandoning 8 fallen and various material useful for the defense while 13 partisans were captured and shot on July 11 together with another 11 Slovenian partisans by the German SS. In Cracova on the wall of the school, there is a plaque that commemorates the 21 shot.}} During the night of June 29–30, the German SS Police Regiment Bozen arrived as reinforcements with two armoured vehicles along the Piedimelze road, the column was blocked by the 18th "Bazoviška" brigade which destroyed an armoured vehicle.
The attack on Koritnica took place at 2 am, initially hit by mortar fire and a hellish fire of automatic weapons, however every attempt to attack was foiled, the cause was that the support group of Alpini and Bersaglieri penetrated the deployment of the 1st battalion of the 3rd "Gradnik" brigade, who hit the partisans of the 2nd battalion from behind who were forced to come out into the open under the crossfire of the Bersaglieri of Koritnica. Following the clash the 1st battalion of the brigade retreated and the second, following heavy losses, climbed up the slope of the Kriška Gora..}} The losses of the 1st battalion of the 3rd "Gradnik" brigade amounted to about 30 killed and wounded, while the 2nd battalion of the same brigade suffered 4 killed and 12 wounded.
The 3rd battalion of the 3rd "Gradnik" brigade had greater success and concentrated its forces in the pillboxes of toll booth 99; supported by mortar fire, it forced the riflemen to take cover. According to Stanko Petelin, in this episode the 2nd and 3rd battalions suffered 11 killed and 10 wounded, while the 1st suffered 3 killed and some wounded.
The 1st battalion of the 16th "Vojko" brigade instead concentrated its efforts on toll booth 107 where about twenty riflemen had the task of defending two railway bridges. However, its efforts were in vain and it had to retreat. During the clashes that took place during the day, the 16th "Vojko" brigade suffered one killed and one wounded due to enemy mortar fire.
Resumption of clashes
On the night of June 29, the partisans resumed their attempts to retake Koritnica. Despite fierce resistance, a Slovenian squad managed to mine the foundations of toll booth 107 and part of the building collapsed. The partisans found 5 dead bersaglieri and one wounded man who was killed on the spot. The partisans took possession of 1 light mortar, 2 heavy machine guns, 2 light machine guns, 9 rifles, 1 pistol and several hand grenades. In one of the bunkers that defended the position, another rifle and a pistol were found. The other survivors managed to escape capture by hiding in the bed of the stream where they managed to reach toll booth 107 bis which had been subjected to bombing for hours. After over 360 kg of explosives the bridge was blown up, and on the Slovenian side 3 men fell.
The German command sent very sparingly 2 armoured cars, 7 light panzers and 2 heavy mortars, to aid the Italians. However, initially only three panzers were actually used, one of which exploded on a mine, losing its entire crew. The other two panzers reached Cracova where they supported the Bersaglieri but were unable to advance. On the evening of the 30th, following insistent requests for help, two platoons of the Polizei arrived from Piedicolle. Due to the slowness with which the Germans brought in reinforcements, the chances of escape for the defenders of the area surrounded by the partisans became increasingly unlikely.
With less and less ammunition, the Bersaglieri had no choice but to try to negotiate to gain time. In the end, after two attacks repelled by the Bersaglieri, they had the worst of it at dawn on July 1st, with the house being blown up as happened to railway box 107. Of the 30 Bersaglieri, only 5 escaped and reached Cracova. cites: "Coritenza resisted for two full days, then fell."}} The 2nd battalion of the 3rd "Gradnik" brigade suffered 7 killed and several wounded in these clashes. The same source assumes double the losses.
Toll booth 99 continued to resist, in this sector the attackers suffered heavy losses. The defenders of the toll booth spotted the Korrnica bersaglieri who had fallen into the hands of the Slovenians; by shooting at the column they created a diversion, in this way 8 Bersaglieri managed to escape their fate by fleeing.
On the 30th, the 19th "Kosovel" brigade also attempted an assault on Kneza, however the weapons the brigade had were not up to the task of those defences, it is difficult to understand why the partisan command did not provide the English anti-tank Piats with which the brigade was equipped, however the attack failed with the toll of 8 dead and 25 wounded, the same source hypothesizes 10 dead and 22 wounded on the part of the defenders.
